editorial_reason: Read Stacks Categories 4.42 Definition 4.42.3. It requires that every 2-fibre product with a category represented by an object of the base is itself representable; this is not the same as representability of an ordinary presheaf natural transformation.

definitions.text: A 1-morphism F:X→Y of categories fibred in groupoids over C is representable when, for every U∈C and every 1-morphism C/U→Y, the 2-fibre product (C/U)×_Y X is a category fibred in groupoids representable by an object over U.
definitions.context_hint: Higher category theory: representable morphism of fibred groupoids

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Commutative Algebra 10.100, whose lemmas characterize how flatness of modules and ring maps persists or descends under flat or local base changes. The chapter uses flatness and base change defined in earlier sections and introduces no separate mathematical object called 'base change and flatness'.

Read Stacks Topology 5.29, which gives explicit coproduct and coequalizer constructions in topological spaces, with a final/quotient topology. The corresponding colimits are different kinds of constructions.

definitions.text: The coproduct of a family (X_i) of topological spaces is their disjoint union with the topology for which U is open exactly when U∩X_i is open in X_i for every index i.
definitions.source_section: Section 5.29, opening construction of topological coproduct
definitions.context_hint: Topology: coproduct or disjoint union topology

definitions.text: For two continuous maps f,g:X⇉Y, their coequalizer in topological spaces is Y modulo the smallest equivalence relation identifying f(x) with g(x) for each x, furnished with the quotient topology.
definitions.context_hint: Topology: topological coequalizer

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Topology 5.26, Definition 5.26.1. The closure-of-open-sets criterion characterizes extremal disconnectedness, which neither presupposes Hausdorffness nor follows from profiniteness alone.

definitions.text: A topological space X is extremally disconnected if the closure of every open subset U of X is itself an open subset of X.
definitions.context_hint: Topology: extremally disconnected space

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.65 Definition 10.65.2. The relative assassin of an S-module refers to associated primes of fibre modules after passing from R to the residue field at the contraction p=q∩R.

definitions.text: For a ring map R→S and S-module N, the relative assassin Ass_{S/R}(N) consists of primes q∈Spec(S) such that q is associated to the fibre module N⊗_R κ(p), where p=q∩R; equivalently q is an associated prime of that S-module.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: relative assassin over a ring map

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Commutative Algebra 10.145, the section on étale local structure of quasi-finite maps. It proves factorization and local-structure statements for already defined quasi-finite and étale ring homomorphisms; no additional standalone mathematical object matching the combined theorem heading is defined.

Read Stacks Topology 5.28, Definitions 5.28.1 through 5.28.4. It gives a locally-closed partition, a stronger good-stratification condition, a stratification with a closure-compatible partial order, and the independent local-finiteness property.

definitions.text: A partition of a topological space X in this setting is a decomposition X=⨆_{i∈I}X_i into pairwise disjoint locally closed subsets whose union is all of X.
definitions.context_hint: Topology: partition into locally closed pieces

definitions.text: A good stratification of X is a partition into locally closed pieces X_i such that, whenever X_i meets the closure of X_j, all of X_i lies in the closure of X_j.
definitions.context_hint: Topology: good stratification

definitions.text: A stratification of X consists of a locally closed partition X=⨆_i X_i and a partial order on the index set such that the closure of X_j lies in the union of pieces X_i with i≤j.
definitions.context_hint: Topology: closure-compatible ordered stratification

definitions.text: A collection (E_i) of subsets of X is locally finite if every x∈X has an open neighbourhood meeting E_i for only finitely many indices i.
definitions.context_hint: Topology: locally finite family of subsets

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Schemes 26.21, Definition 26.21.3. It defines separatedness and quasi-separatedness of a morphism through closed and quasi-compact diagonals, and extends both to absolute scheme properties.

definitions.text: A morphism f:X→S of schemes is separated if its diagonal morphism Δ_{X/S}:X→X×_S X is a closed immersion.
definitions.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: separated scheme morphism

definitions.text: A scheme morphism f:X→S is quasi-separated if the diagonal map X→X×_S X is quasi-compact.
definitions.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: quasi-separated scheme morphism

definitions.text: A scheme X is separated (respectively quasi-separated) if its structure morphism to Spec(Z) is separated (respectively quasi-separated).
definitions.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: separatedness of a scheme

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Fields 9.24, introductory Kummer construction and Lemma 9.24.1. Under the hypothesis that the base field contains the relevant nth roots of unity and char(K) does not divide n, adjoining an nth root yields a cyclic Galois extension.

definitions.text: In the Kummer setting, an extension L/K is obtained by adjoining an element α satisfying α^n=a∈K, where n≥2 is prime to char(K) and K contains the nth roots of unity; when [L:K] is finite, L/K is a cyclic Galois extension of degree dividing n.
definitions.context_hint: Field theory: Kummer extension generated by an nth root

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Fields 9.4, introductory identification of a field module with a vector space. It treats the underlying algebraic object as a module over a field and proves such modules are free.

definitions.text: A vector space over a field k is an abelian group V together with scalar multiplication k×V→V satisfying distributivity, scalar associativity, and the condition 1·v=v; equivalently V is a unital module over k.
definitions.source_section: Section 9.4 opening paragraph (modules over a field)
definitions.context_hint: Linear algebra: vector space over a field

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Commutative Algebra 10.55, which explicitly constructs two Grothendieck groups: one from finite modules with exact-sequence relations and the other from finite projective modules. They differ in general.

definitions.text: For a ring R, K′_0(R) is the abelian group generated by isomorphism classes [M] of finitely generated R-modules, subject to [M]=[M′]+[M″] for every short exact sequence 0→M′→M→M″→0 of finitely generated modules.
definitions.context_hint: Algebraic K-theory: Grothendieck group of finite modules

definitions.text: For a ring R, K_0(R) is the abelian group generated by finite projective R-modules up to isomorphism, modulo [P⊕Q]=[P]+[Q], equivalently modulo split short exact sequence relations among these modules.
definitions.context_hint: Algebraic K-theory: Grothendieck group of finite projective modules

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Schemes 26.22, Lemmas 26.22.1 and 26.22.2. The uniqueness part of the valuative criterion is a precise lifting property for valuation rings and implies separatedness under the quasi-separated hypothesis.

definitions.text: A scheme morphism f:X→S satisfies the uniqueness part of the valuative criterion if, for every valuation ring V with fraction field K and every commutative diagram Spec(K)→X, Spec(V)→S, there is at most one morphism Spec(V)→X making both triangles commute.
definitions.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: valuative uniqueness condition for separatedness

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Commutative Algebra 10.156, a series of lemmas on compatibility of henselization or strict henselization with quotients and quasi-finite local ring extensions. Henselization and quasi-finiteness are already defined in their respective source sections; this page supplies compatibility theorems but no new named object.

Read Stacks 10.59, Definitions 10.59.1, 10.59.6 and the opening Hilbert–Samuel function construction. Its distinct definitions concern ideals of definition and Hilbert polynomials of finite modules over local Noetherian rings.

definitions.text: For a Noetherian local ring (R,m), an ideal I⊆R is an ideal of definition when its radical is the maximal ideal m, equivalently I is m-primary.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: ideal of definition of a local ring

definitions.text: For a finite R-module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,m), its Hilbert–Samuel length function is χ_M(n)=length_R(M/m^{n+1}M) for nonnegative integers n.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: Hilbert–Samuel function

definitions.text: For a finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,m), the Hilbert polynomial is the rational-coefficient polynomial P such that P(n)=length_R(m^nM/m^{n+1}M) for all sufficiently large n.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: Hilbert polynomial of a finite local module

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Schemes 26.19, Definition 26.19.1 and Lemma 26.19.2. Quasi-compact scheme morphisms are characterized by quasi-compact inverse images of affine target opens.

definitions.text: A morphism f:X→S of schemes is quasi-compact if the inverse image of each quasi-compact open subset of S is quasi-compact in X; it suffices to test affine open subsets of S.
definitions.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: quasi-compact morphism of schemes

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Topology 5.10, Definitions 5.10.1 and 5.10.5. Dimension of a space, dimension at a point and equidimensionality are distinct mathematical notions defined with chains of irreducible closed subsets.

definitions.text: The Krull dimension of a topological space X is the supremum of lengths of strict finite chains of irreducible closed subsets of X, taking dimension −∞ for the empty space.
definitions.context_hint: Topology: Krull dimension of a topological space

definitions.text: For a point x in a topological space X, the local Krull dimension dim_x(X) is the minimum of dim(U) over all open neighbourhoods U of x.
definitions.context_hint: Topology: local Krull dimension at a point

definitions.text: A topological space X is equidimensional if all of its irreducible components have the same Krull dimension.
definitions.context_hint: Topology: equidimensional topological space
